title: Poison Valleys: Diagnosing Path-Dependent Failure in LLM Code Repair
abstract: arXiv:2610.21514v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: When code-repair agents fail, final tests reveal that a patch is wrong but not which earlier commitment caused it or which software obligation failed. Poison Valleys traces this path in 1,844 model requests on two synthetic Python cases: PersistQueue adds atomic batch claiming to a disk-backed queue, while Dijkstra adds source-sensitive filtering to shortest-path search. We define plausible but incorrect software mechanisms, place each in a model's hypothesis, implementation plan, or both, and evaluate the generated code with an Oracle and targeted diagnostic coordinates. Moving the misconception from hypothesis to plan increased failure by 32.2% in PersistQueue and 28.9% in Dijkstra after matching the experimental mix. Different misconceptions produced distinct, model-dependent patterns of violated obligations, although several could converge on the same behavior. This creates a measured connection from upstream misconception to code

translated_title: 毒谷：诊断LLM代码修复中的路径依赖性失败
translated_abstract: 当代码修复智能体失败时，最终测试只能揭示补丁是错误的，但无法说明是哪一个早期的承诺导致了失败，或哪个软件义务未能满足。Poison Valleys 在两个合成 Python 案例的 1,844 次模型请求中追踪了这一失败路径：PersistQueue 为基于磁盘的队列添加原子批量认领功能，Dijkstra 则为最短路径搜索添加源敏感过滤功能。我们定义了看似合理但不正确的软件机制，将每种错误概念分别置于模型的假设、实现计划或两者之中，并使用 Oracle 和有针对性的诊断坐标来评估生成的代码。在匹配实验组合后，将错误概念从假设阶段移至计划阶段使 PersistQueue 的失败率增加了 32.2%，Dijkstra 的失败率增加了 28.9%。不同的错误概念产生了独特的、依赖模型的具体义务违反模式，尽管其中若干错误可能收敛于相同的行为。这建立了从上游错误概念到代码失败之间的量化联系。
tldr: 该论文提出“毒谷”诊断框架，通过向LLM代码修复的假设与计划中注入看似合理但错误的软件机制，首次量化揭示了上游错误概念的位置如何路径依赖性地决定下游代码失败——将错误概念从假设移至计划阶段会使失败率增加约29%至32%。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces "Poison Valleys," a diagnostic framework that injects plausible-but-wrong software mechanisms into LLM code repair hypotheses and plans across 1,844 model requests, quantitatively establishing the path-dependent connection between upstream misconception placement and downstream code failures—shifting a misconception from hypothesis to plan increased failure rates by 29–32%.
